thread:
rachel: quick post - last night's EU dedicated pool showed sustained "back-and-forth" scaling when several tenants spiked simultaneously. pattern: admission -> promotion -> scaler launch -> drop -> repeat. :grimacing:
ben: saw it. looks like the promotion path is too eager when cloud cold-start latency is high. we inflate node count before we converge on real demand.
katie: idea: introduce a promotion-queue with backpressure credits. admission queues promotion intents and consumes credits; autoscaler pulls intents but only consumes credits when it actually commits nodes. credits decay if not used.
marco: sketch of semantics:

```
promotion_queue:
  credit_bucket: 20p
  per_tenant_reserve: 4p
  credit_decay: 0.2  # per minute
  promote_window: 60s
  pull_batch_max: 3 intents
```

rachel: key goals: 1) reduce warmup churn, 2) make promotion a pull-based contract (autoscaler pulls, doesn't get surprised), 3) surface when promotions are queued vs executed.
diana: operationally important: add "promotion_snapshot" traces so we can correlate queued intents -> pulled intents -> node_launch. also add metric promotion_queue_depth{tenant} and queued_credit_fraction.
katie: fairness question: how do we ensure small tenants aren't starved by big ones? proposal: a weighted fairness algorithm that guarantees a minimum per-tenant reserve and then pro-rata allocation for extra credits. hard cap per tenant to prevent abuse.
ben: billing question: do we bill for queued promotions? i'd prefer not to bill queued credits until they convert to nodes, but mark events with billing_tag=queued so product can later choose.
marco: autoscaler-side behavior: when pulling intents, it should consider cost-weighted packing hints in intent (bin-packing score), and prefer to batch-promote compatible intents to reduce cold starts. e.g., pack 3 small intents into 1 node if profiles allow.
rachel: we also need a backpressure circuit: if overall queued_credit_fraction > 0.75 for >5m, escalate: either 1) force-promote some intents with lower-cost profiles, or 2) trigger operator alert. config knob for automatic escalation.
diana: sequences to capture in traces:
- admit -> queue intent (intent_id)
- promotion_snapshot at time T (queue depth, credits)
- autoscaler_pull(id list) -> would_launch decision
- node_launch -> intent_consumed event
- intent_stale or intent_expire

scale-bot: canary scheduled for 2951243600. mode: dry-run for 12h at 2% traffic, then active for 3% if no regressions.
katie: test plan: run sims with historical traces; vary credit_bucket in [10,20,40], promote_window in [30s,60s,120s], and pull_batch_max [1,3,5]. measure churn, wasted warmup cost, tail latency.
ben: ops alert set: promotion_queue_depth_total > 50 for >10m OR queued_credit_fraction > 0.8 for >5m -> page SRE. also add a grafana panel with promotion lifecycle waterfall per-tenant.
marco: edge-cases:
- intent ttl expires while queued: emit intent_stale metric and allow admission to refresh with jittered retry.
- autoscaler blackout (can't pull): admission must cap new promotions and optionally fall back to throttling policy.
- packing conflicts: when two intents want incompatible profiles, autoscaler should honor priority_hint and avoid bad packing.

rachel: UX: console should show per-tenant queue position, queued credits, last_intent_ts, and "likely_action" (will_promote|likely_throttle). helpful for SEs and CS.
diana: add a dry-run flag to intents and an autoscaler would_launch trace that always emits decision but doesn't act. that's our canary first phase.
katie: security note: intents must be signed by admission and carry monotonic id to avoid dupes. autoscaler must dedupe by intent_id and idempotency_token.
ben: rollout steps draft:
1) admission: add promotion_queue + metrics + signed intent ids (katie)
2) autoscaler: implement pull API + would_launch traces + packing heuristics (marco)
3) sims: run 90-day replay and tune knobs (rachel)
4) canary: dry-run 2% -> active 3% (scale-bot/rachel)
5) monitor alerts & iterate

marco: small optimization: when packing multiple intents into one node, emit a packing_hint so billing and tracing can apportion cost. also prefer pre-warmed small-instance pools for fast-promotes.
rachel: agreed. also let's ensure the promotion_queue supports a "priority lane" for urgent intents from enterprise customers. priority lanes consume reserved credits but bypass some packing rules.
diana: will add metrics: promotion_queue_latency_ms, promotion_queue_discarded_count, intent_retry_count. ops will have runbook: "if queue depth high, check packing failures, check cloud provision latency, consider bumping pre-warmed pool."
scale-bot: noted - canary scheduled and monitoring hooks created.
ben: any blocking concerns?
katie: only ask: ensure we don't introduce a single-point queue bottleneck. design queue as distributed per-shard with consistent hashing by tenant.
marco: agreed, implement queue sharding and a global coordinator for reserved credits.
rachel: OK next steps: katie and marco implement core pieces, diana add dashboards & alerts, ben draft playbook. i'll open RFC PR with DSL, sequence diagram, and sample Grafana. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
